findings.summary: guard-config was silenced for all 108 edits under tools/guard/ (`rules_off: ["guard-config"]` in the container). That ask is the guard's own change control. The only record of the 108 `skipped` lines is the container's decision log, "which goes with the container", and the owner's permission sits only in a session transcript. Under ALCOA+, the evidence that the control was bypassed is not kept with the change. Fix before merge: export the skipped lines and a quote of the owner's dialog into the PR or the repo, or justify why that is not needed.

The agent merges before #50's own acceptance criterion 6 has run: the 45-day replay checking that nothing got weaker, plus the count of new prompts. Also not run: the 3.9 interpreter (CI only), the hook timing on the owner's machine, and `tracker.py review`. The block names all of these as owed, but the change is a regulated control and its validation evidence is incomplete at merge. Either hold the merge until the replay has run, or have the owner sign off on the PR.

`if "<<" not in text or "\x00" in text: return strip_heredocs(text)`: one NUL character anywhere in the command turns off here-document-as-script reading for the whole line. DECISIONS (line 325) records that bash and sh drop the NUL and run the rest from stdin, so `bash <<EOF` holding `git commit --no-verify` plus a NUL is silent. It is no weaker than 0.7.1, but there is no test for it, and answering a NUL in a shell command with an ask would close it at almost no cost.

`CHAIN_BOUND_S = 1.0` is checked against `time.perf_counter()` (line 1084). This makes a correctness test depend on how fast the runner is, so it can fail by chance on a loaded CI agent (the DECISIONS block already notes this). The bound is better expressed as a work count, such as reads per hop, than as wall-clock time.

summary: Guard 0.8.0, group A. The diff removes no tests and loosens no assertions. The new readers are checked through about 800 table rows, and none of the reviewed paths is weaker than 0.7.1. That includes the ask-before-deny ordering in rule_git_guard, now collected and combined. No secrets or client data appear. The verdict is COMMENT, not APPROVE, for three reasons. First, the merge happens before the acceptance replay (criterion 6 of #50) and before any local Python 3.9 run. Second, the guard-config change-control ask was switched off for the whole build, and the evidence for that leaves with the container. Third, there is a known bypass of the new fed-script reader: a NUL character in the command. It is no weaker than 0.7.1, but it has no test and there is an easy stricter answer. A flaky wall-clock test is a minor point.
